best_for: People who want a ChatGPT-style chat window on their own computer, running open models offline, with the option to plug in a cloud model when a local one falls short.
description:
Jan is a desktop app for chatting with AI models, made by Menlo Research and built in public on GitHub. You need no account. On first launch it downloads a default model of its own, so you can start typing right away.

The Hub tells you whether a model fits your hardware before you download it. Built-in web search lets you ask about today's news. Assistants save a set of instructions, such as "keep answers short", so you stop repeating yourself, and Projects group chats that share instructions and files. Cowork, still in preview, takes a task and works through files, commands and web research on its own.

points.title: Local models first
points.text: Jan downloads open models such as Llama, Gemma and Qwen from Hugging Face and runs them on your machine. Chats can stay on the computer, and the project says Jan can work fully offline.

points.title: Cloud models with your own key
points.text: You can also connect hosted models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Groq and others. Those requests leave your machine and are billed by that provider, not by Jan.

points.title: A local API for other apps
points.text: Jan can run a server on port 1337 that speaks the OpenAI API format. Scripts and tools built for OpenAI can point at it and use your local model instead.

points.title: RAM decides which models fit
points.text: The README suggests about 8 GB of RAM for 3B models, 16 GB for 7B and 32 GB for 13B. Macs need macOS 13.6 or later; on Windows 10 and later it can use NVIDIA, AMD and Intel Arc GPUs.

points.title: Free, with MCP built in
points.text: Jan is free and open source. It includes MCP connectors, so a model can call outside tools. Memory of your preferences is still marked as coming soon on the home page.

points.title: Large Linux download
points.text: The Flathub build is published by Menlo Research, which Flathub marks as verified, but it is x64 only and about 685 MB to download. The project also offers .deb and AppImage files.

points.title: Older versions live on Windows
points.text: The Windows installer is per-user and needs no administrator rights. The Windows listing keeps 45 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
